context: Characterization of the two SQL primitives first. Two small prototypes in a branch or appendix, then a short ADR under docs/development/adr/. No production fold of cloud adapters in this item.
description:
DECISION GATE. Do not start a repo-wide injection campaign before this ADR lands.

Declared layering is utils < core < platforms < cli (.importlinter). Implemented layering allowlists ~34 core→platforms edges including runner.runner, platform_registry→platforms.base, and dryrun→platforms. run_service already injects AdapterFactory; runner.py still imports get_platform_adapter.

Option A: finish 'core is kernel' with protocols and injection; delete allowlisted edges incrementally.
Option B: introduce benchbox.runtime above core and platforms as the composition layer. benchbox/runtime does not exist today — B is greenfield.

Prototype requirement: one of the two prototypes MUST be the SQL execute/validate edge. It already straddles the boundary:
- CursorValidationQueryExecutionMixin in benchbox/core/benchmark_mixins.py:159 (inheritance, logs PASS/FAIL, always connection.cursor(), no rollback, no result digest)
- execute_sql_query in benchbox/platforms/base/sql_execution.py:49 (injected callables, rollback, result digest, pre-created cursor, validation without PASS/FAIL logs)

Those two disagree on observable behavior. Folding either way without choosing a home layer is the defect this ADR prevents.

Second prototype: one runner edge (remove get_platform_adapter from runner.py behind the existing factory) OR one DataFrame edge. Do not invent a synthetic example.

Stop condition: the ADR names (1) the winning option, (2) the winning SQL primitive's home layer, (3) the deletion order for allowlisted core→platforms edges. If neither option survives both prototypes, record that outcome and stop — do not invent Option C as a mechanical core split.

Does not block arch-delete-dead-setup-lifecycle-fork or arch-docs-truth-refresh.

anti_patterns.why: two incumbents already disagree; a third is more drift
the plugin-seam doc rejects mechanical core splits
